answers.answer: SCOPe places all three in family a.298.1.1 because the family is defined by homology of the repeated unit, not by the total number of repeats present in a given structure. In SCOPe 2.08, d2kq5a_ (PthA, Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri, 51 residues), d3v6pa_ (dHax3, Xanthomonas, 373 residues) and d4cj9a_ (BurrH, Burkholderia rhizoxinica, 752 residues) share the full lineage: class a (all alpha), fold a.298 (left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix, sunid 267589), superfamily a.298.1 (TAL effector-like, sunid 267596), family a.298.1.1 (TAL effector, sunid 267609), with separate protein nodes (sunids 267645, 267646, 267647). The lengths differ roughly 15-fold only because each structure contains a different count of the same roughly 34-residue two-helix hairpin repeat. SCOPe records this explicitly: the family's canonical repeat unit is defined on the BurrH representative as 4cj9 A:259-292, and that one repeat definition is propagated to every member. d2kq5a_ carries the curator comment 'single repeat' (the 2kq5 NMR structure is a minimal PthA fragment of about one and a half repeats), dHax3 in 3v6p is a designed array of about eleven and a half repeats, and BurrH in 4cj9 is a full-length protein with roughly twenty repeats. d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_ also carry the SCOPe 're' inconsistency flag, whose definition states that it applies to all domains of a family when the common domain is composed of a different number of small repeating units; this is SCOPe's formal acknowledgement that domain length within this family is variable by design. Because the repeat is the unit of homology and successive repeats stack into one continuous superhelix, SCOPe keeps the entire chain as a single domain (the '_' SID suffix) rather than cutting it into per-repeat domains, so sequence length is simply repeat count times unit length. Family membership is further supported by clear sequence similarity between the repeat units (the Xanthomonas TALE repeats are nearly identical to each other apart from the repeat-variable di-residue positions, and BurrH repeats are recognisably related though more divergent) plus shared superhelical architecture. Caveats: shared fold a.298 alone would not establish homology, but here membership is at family level, the strongest SCOPe assertion of common ancestry. Function should not be transferred naively across members: DNA-binding specificity depends on repeat number and on the variable di-residue in each repeat, and BurrH is a TALE-like protein from a different genus whose repeat specificity differs; d2kq5a_ is too short to bind DNA on its own and is a poor template for full arrays, whereas d4cj9a_ is the representative on which the repeat boundaries are defined. Also, 2kq5 is an NMR fragment and 4cj9 carries a selenium-labelled annotation, so representative choice for modelling should weigh these differences.
